intro.title: Build typed permissions DSL
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed permissions Domain-Specific Language (DSL) in TypeScript. You will create a system that defines user roles and actions, then checks if a user is allowed to perform an action based on their role. The core concept is using TypeScript's type system to enforce permissions at compile time, making your code safer and more predictable. You'll work with TypeScript interfaces, union types, and generic functions to construct this DSL. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe permissions checker that can be integrated into applications.
intro.usecase: A typed permissions DSL is essential for building secure, maintainable authorization systems in enterprise applications. You'll find this pattern in admin dashboards where different user roles (admin, editor, viewer) need granular access controls to features, data, and UI components. SaaS platforms like project management tools or CRM systems use typed permissions to define who can create projects, edit customer records, or view financial reports. By implementing a type-safe DSL, developers prevent runtime authorization errors and ensure permissions logic is explicit and testable throughout the application.
